title: Crohn’s disease Longitudinal Evaluation of Anti-fibrotic Response to UPadacitinib
official: Crohn’s disease Longitudinal Evaluation of Anti-fibrotic Response to UPadacitinib
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the effect of upadacitinib on small bowel strictures in patients with Crohn’s disease, using MRI-based assessment at week 24.
conditions: Crohn’s disease with ileal stricturing complication
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients with Crohn’s disease with stricturing complications
2. Voluntary written informed consent of the participant or their legally authorized representative has been obtained prior to any Screening procedures
3. Adult subjects (age ≥18 and < 80)
4. Patients with endoscopically reachable small bowel strictures, max 2 strictures.
5. Naïve or anastomotic small bowel strictures (not in the stricturoplasty) assessed on MRE with   * localized luminal narrowing ≤50% relative to normal adjacent bowel (assuming a normal bowel lumen diameter measurement of 20mm; a lumen diameter measurement within a stricture of ≤10mm is required).  AND   * bowel wall thickening  (BWT) ≥25% relative to adjacent bowel (assuming that the normal thickness of the small intestine is ≤3mm, an average maximal stricture bowel wall thickness measurement of ≥4mm is required).
Exclusion criteria:
1. Participant has a history of primary non-response, secondary loss of response or intolerance to upadacitinib
2. Patients having any contraindications to MRE assessment
3. Small bowel obstruction with anticipated surgery within 2 weeks
4. Patients requiring endoscopic balloon dilation at screening
5. Concomitant internal fistula’s and/or collections linked to the stricture on MR enterography
6. Strictures that, based on MRE, are suspected to be malignant
7. Single focal (< 1 cm) anastomic strictures
8. Any disorder, which in the Investigator’s opinion might jeopardise the participant’s safety or compliance with the protocol
9. Any prior or concomitant treatment(s) that might jeopardise the participant’s safety or that would compromise the integrity of the Trial
10. Any other factors that might jeopardise the participant’s safety or integrity of the trial (e.g. non-compliance).
11. Participation in an interventional Trial with an Investigational Medicinal Product (IMP) or device
12. Patients with an ostomy
13. Patients with colonic stenosis
14. Patients with ulcerative colitis or inflammatory bowel disease type unclassified
15. Participant has a formal contraindication for JAK inhibition or patients presenting with criteria in the warnings and precautions section in the SmpC
